html:
Sobhuza I, also called Somhlolo, was the king who led the Ngwane people north into what is now Eswatini in the early 19th century and founded the Swazi kingdom there.

Pressed by the Ndwandwe and other rising powers during the wars of the Mfecane, he moved his people from the Pongola river into the hills of the centre. He absorbed the clans living there, often by marriage, and avoided war with the Zulu kingdom of Shaka by sending gifts and wives.

He is remembered for a dream in which pale-skinned people came carrying a book and money, read as a warning to accept the Bible but avoid war with Europeans. His son Mswati II built the kingdom into a military power. The national stadium of Eswatini bears his name.
sum: Sobhuza I, also called Somhlolo, was the king who led the Ngwane people north into what is now Eswatini in the early 19th century and founded the Swazi kingdom there.
